questions.stem: A 28-year-old man presents to the emergency department with complaints of palpitations, tremors, and sweating after a sudden fright. His blood glucose level is checked and found to be elevated. The physician explains that this is due to the combined action of epinephrine and glucagon on liver glycogen metabolism, which rapidly mobilizes glucose to meet the increased energy demand. Which of the following best describes their effect on glycogen metabolism in the liver?

options.label: A
options.text: cAMP-dependent tyrosine kinase A is activated,

options.label: B
options.text: Glycogen phosphorylase is phosphorylated and active, whereas glycogen synthase is phosphorylated and inactive

options.label: C
options.text: The net synthesis of glycogen is increased

options.label: D
options.text: Both glycogen phosphorylase and glycogen synthase are activated by phosphorylation but at significantly different rates

questions.answerText: Glycogen phosphorylase is phosphorylated and active, whereas glycogen synthase is phosphorylated and inactive
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Glycogen phosphorylase is phosphorylated and active, whereas glycogen synthase is phosphorylated and inactive

questions.stem: A 30-year-old male presents with fatigue, pallor, and jaundice following an episode of fever. His blood smear shows bite cells and Heinz bodies. The physician explains that mature red blood cells lack a nucleus and mitochondria, and therefore rely entirely on glycolysis and the HMP shunt for energy and redox balance. Which of the following is not present in mature RBCs?

A 52-year-old male with a history of smoking presents with weight loss, chronic cough, and hemoptysis. CT chest shows a suspicious lung mass. On biopsy, the tumor shows increased expression of p53, which activates a protein called TIGAR. Which of the following statements about TIGAR is correct?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) All of the above

questions.stem: Assertion: Malate shuttle is required for glycolysis Reason: In Gluconeogenesis NADH is transported from mitochondria to cytoplasm
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) A and R both correct

questions.stem: A young man finds that every time he eats dairy products, he feels very uncomfortable. His stomach becomes distended. He develops gas and diarrhea frequently. These symptoms donot appear when he eats food other than dairy products. Which of the following is most likely enzyme in which this young man is deficient

A 24-year-old athlete collapses during an intense 400-meter sprint. Laboratory evaluation reveals accumulation of lactate in his blood. The physician explains that during anaerobic conditions, glycolysis must continue despite limited oxygen. For this to happen, NAD⁺ must be regenerated so that glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (a key enzyme in glycolysis) can function. Which of the following enzymes is primarily responsible for regenerating NAD⁺ under anaerobic glycolysis?

A 3-year-old child is brought with complaints of seizures, irritability, and sweating during fasting. Examination reveals severe hepatomegaly and doll-like facies. Laboratory findings show fasting hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, hyperuricemia, and hyperlipidemia. The hypoglycemia does not improve after glucagon injection. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Pyruvate, a key intermediate, can undergo several fates depending on cellular needs and oxygen availability. Pyruvate can be converted directly to all of the following except:

questions.stemHtml: Which reaction in the diagram below would be inhibited in the presence of large amounts of avidin, an egg white protein that binds and sequesters biotin?

questions.stem: A 5-month-old boy is brought to his physician because of vomiting, night sweats, and tremors. History revealed that these symptoms began after fruit juices were introduced to his diet as he was being weaned off breast milk. The physical examination was remarkable for hepatomegaly. Tests on the baby’s urine were positive for reducing sugar but negative for glucose. The infant most likely suffers from a deficiency of:

A sprinter is trying to optimize his performance. He has calculated that, even under anaerobic conditions, his glycogen stores will supply him with enough energy to last the race. What would the energy difference be between using glucose from a dietary source versus relying solely on glucose from glycogen stores as fuel for his race?

options.label: A
options.text: Dietary would give 1 more mole of ATP/glucose

options.label: B
options.text: Dietary would give 2 more moles of ATP/ glucose

options.label: C
options.text: Dietary would give the same ATP/glucose

options.label: D
options.text: Dietary would give 1 less mole of ATP/ glucose

questions.answerText: Dietary would give 1 less mole of ATP/ glucose
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Dietary would give 1 less mole of ATP/ glucose

questions.stem: A teenager suffering from type V glycogen storage disease is getting examined by a rubber ball squeezing test while exercising her forearm. Which of following statements will be true for this patient compared to a normal person?

options.label: A
options.text: ↑ blood glucose in the blood drawn from the exercising forearm vein

options.label: C
options.text: ↑ blood lactate in the blood drawn from the exercising forearm vein

options.label: D
options.text: Relatively ↓ blood lactate in the blood drawn from the exercising forearm vein

questions.answerText: Relatively ↓ blood lactate in the blood drawn from the exercising forearm vein
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Relatively ↓ blood lactate in the blood drawn from the exercising forearm vein

questions.stem: A 35-year-old individual who consumed fast food from a street vendor for several days recently comes to a hospital with continuous vomiting over the last 12 hours. Despite not being able to eat or drink much, the patient's blood glucose levels remain stable. Which organ has played the primary role in maintaining this individual's blood glucose level in this duration?

Two children are brought to a pediatric metabolic clinic for evaluation of abnormal fructose metabolism.Child 1: Develops severe hypoglycemia, vomiting, and hepatomegaly after consuming fruit juices. The doctor advises the parents to strictly restrict dietary fructose.Child 2: Has fructose detected in blood and urine during routine screening, but remains asymptomatic even after fructose intake. The doctor reassures the parents that no dietary restriction is required.Which enzyme conversion is most likely deficient in Child 2?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Conversion of fructose into fructose-1-phosphate

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman is advised by her dietitian to increase intake of prebiotics in her diet to improve gut health. She is prescribed supplements containing inulin-like fructans. The physician explains that these compounds are not digested in the upper gastrointestinal tract, which allows them to reach the colon and act as prebiotics.Assertion (A): Inulin-like fructans are used as probiotics as they are non-digestible.Reason (R): Resistance to digestion in the upper GI tract results from the β-configuration at the anomeric carbon (C2).Which one of the following is correct?

options.label: B
options.text: A and R both correct but R is not the explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: Both A and R are wrong

options.label: D
options.text: A and R both correct and R is the correct explanation of A

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man accidentally ingests a contaminated herbal preparation. Within a few hours, he develops severe fatigue, muscle weakness, and lactic acidosis. He is admitted to the ICU, where further studies reveal that ATP synthesis in his mitochondria is severely inhibited. The toxic compound in the preparation is later identified as oligomycin, an antibiotic produced by Streptomyces species. Which of the following statements about the mechanism of action of oligomycin is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: It reduces electron flow through the electron transport chain

options.label: C
options.text: It has no action on the F1 subunit

options.label: D
options.text: It activates the proton channel (Fo subunit)

questions.answerText: It activates the proton channel (Fo subunit)
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) It activates the proton channel (Fo subunit)

questions.stem: A 19-year-old college athlete is evaluated after repeated complaints of excessive urination and thirst during practice sessions. His blood glucose and HbA1c are normal. A glucose tolerance test is also normal. Urinalysis, however, consistently shows the presence of glucose only, with no ketones or other sugars detected. Family history reveals his father had similar findings on routine medical exams. Which of the following transporter deficiencies best explains this condition?

A student takes some tablets she is offered at a disco, and without asking what they are she swallows them. A short time later she starts to hyperventilate and becomes very hot. What is the most likely action of the tablets she has taken?

options.label: A
options.text: An inhibitor of mitochondrial ATP synthesis

options.label: B
options.text: An inhibitor of the transport of ADP into mitochondria to be phosphorylated

options.label: C
options.text: An inhibitor of the transport of ATP out of mitochondria into the cytosol

options.label: D
options.text: An uncoupler of mitochondrial electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation

questions.answerText: An uncoupler of mitochondrial electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) An uncoupler of mitochondrial electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation

questions.stem: Which of the following metabolic intermediate involved in glycolysis, gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis

A 25-year-old man is found to have persistent reducing substances in his urine during a routine health checkup. However, his blood glucose levels are consistently normal. Further biochemical analysis confirms a benign inborn error of carbohydrate metabolism due to a deficiency of the enzyme xylulose reductase. Which substance is excreted in excess in his urine?
Which of the following is accumulated in joint in the mucopolysaccharidosis associated with Natowicz disease?

A 60-year-old patient is diagnosed with a rapidly growing tumor. PET scan shows high glucose uptake in the cancerous tissue. This increased glucose consumption occurs even when oxygen is present. Which of the following mechanisms best explains this phenomenon in cancer cells?

options.label: B
options.text: Increased pyruvate to acetyl CoA (high NADH/NAD⁺ ratio)

options.label: C
options.text: Enhanced conversion of glucose to pyruvate

options.label: D
options.text: Lactic acid is produced despite the presence of oxygen

questions.answerText: Lactic acid is produced despite the presence of oxygen
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Lactic acid is produced despite the presence of oxygen

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy is admitted to the hospital with prolonged fasting. During fasting, the body uses ketone bodies as an alternate fuel source. One of the key reactions in ketone body utilization is:Succinyl CoA + Acetoacetate → Acetoacetyl CoA + SuccinateThis reaction is catalyzed by thiophorase (succinyl-CoA: acetoacetate CoA transferase).In which of the following tissues does this reaction not occur?

Assertion: When the liver is actively synthesizing fatty acids in fed state, there is a concomitant decrease in β oxidation of fatty acids inside the mitochondria.Reason: Malonyl coA inhibit CPT-1, present at outer mitochondrial membrane.

options.label: A
options.text: A and R both correct and R is explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: A and R both correct but R is not explanation of A

questions.answerText: A and R both correct and R is explanation of A

questions.stemHtml: Niemann-Pick disease, like other neurolipidoses, present in infancy or childhood with plateauing of development and neurologic regression. The accumulating substance is a phospholipid made in which of the following steps in the figure below?
Select the one best answer A= inner mitochondrial membrane B= mitochondrial matrix C= outer mitochondrial membrane Select the appropriate location from the drawing shown above.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) HMG – CoA lyase – B

questions.stem: A young patient with a history of recurring attacks of pancreatitis, eruptive xanthomas, normal cholesterol, and increased plasma triglyceride levels (1500 mg/dl) associated with chylomicrons, most likely has a deficiency in:

A 40-year-old man has been fasting for 3 days as part of a religious ritual. On examination, he has mild weakness but is otherwise stable. His blood glucose is maintained within the normal range due to gluconeogenesis. However, large amounts of acetyl-CoA are being generated from fatty acid β-oxidation. During this prolonged starvation state, the majority of acetyl-CoA is diverted for which metabolic process?

A 17-year-old girl presents with progressive difficulty in night vision, unsteady gait, and tingling sensations in her hands and feet. On examination, she has retinitis pigmentosa, absent ankle reflexes, and a wide-based ataxic gait. Nerve conduction studies reveal peripheral neuropathy. Laboratory investigations show markedly elevated phytanic acid levels in the blood. Which of the following disorders best explains her condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Refsum disease 



sum disease

questions.stem: Presence of ketonuria and absence of glycosuria are the essential clinical manifestations in one of the following conditions?

questions.stemHtml: A 2-year-old boy presents with progressive hepatosplenomegaly, developmental delay, and loss of motor milestones. On examination, he has hypotonia and a cherry-red spot on the macula. A bone marrow aspirate shows the presence of foam cells (lipid-laden macrophages). Which of the following storage disorders best explains these findings?

questions.stem: A low-level carbon dioxide labeled with C14 is accidentally released into the atmosphere surrounding industrial workers as they resume work following the lunch hour. Unknowingly, they breathe the contaminated air for 1 hour. Which of the following compounds will be radioactively labeled?

options.label: A
options.text: All of the carbon atoms of newly synthesized fatty acid.

options.label: B
options.text: About one half of the carbon atoms of newly synthesized fatty acids.

options.label: C
options.text: About one third of the carbons of newly synthesized malonyl CoA.

options.label: D
options.text: One half of the carbon atoms of newly synthesized acetyl CoA.

questions.answerText: About one third of the carbons of newly synthesized malonyl CoA.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) About one third of the carbons of newly synthesized malonyl CoA.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man begins a ketogenic diet rich in fats and very low in carbohydrates. After 48 hours of fasting, his body switches predominantly to fatty acid oxidation for energy. During β-oxidation of fatty acids in the mitochondria, a specific sequence of enzymes acts repeatedly on the acyl-CoA chain to release acetyl-CoA units. Which of the following correctly lists the enzymes involved in this sequential process?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Dehydrogenase, hydratase, dehydrogenase, thiolase

questions.stem: One specific enzyme participates in cholesterol synthesis, ketone body synthesis, and β-oxidation of fatty acids, making it central to multiple metabolic pathways. Which of the following is this enzyme?

Fatty acids are broken down by repeated removal of two carbon fragments as acetyl-CoA in the β-oxidation cycle, and synthesized by repeated condensation of acetyl-CoAs until a long-chain saturated fatty acid with an even number of carbons is formed. Since fatty acids need to be broken down when energy is in short supply and synthesized when it is plentiful, there are important differences between the two processes which help cells to regulate them efficiently. Which one of the following statements concerning these differences is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Fatty acid breakdown takes place inside mitochondria, while synthesis occurs in the cytosol.

options.label: B
options.text: Fatty acid breakdown uses NAD and produces NADH, while synthesis uses NADPH and produces NADP.

options.label: C
options.text: Transport across the mitochondrial membrane of fatty acyl groups is required for fatty acid breakdown, but not for synthesis.

options.label: D
options.text: Glucagon promotes fatty acid synthesis and inhibits fatty acid breakdown.

questions.answerText: Glucagon promotes fatty acid synthesis and inhibits fatty acid breakdown.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Glucagon promotes fatty acid synthesis and inhibits fatty acid breakdown.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man presents with severe hypercholesterolemia and normal triglyceride level. He reports that several of his close relatives died of myocardial infarction or stroke at a young age. Genetic testing is being considered for a suspected inherited lipid disorder. A decreased function of which of the following genes is most likely responsible for his condition?

A 28-year-old man presents to the emergency department with profuse watery diarrhea after returning from a coastal village outbreak. Stool culture grows Vibrio cholerae. The physician explains that the severe fluid loss is due to a bacterial toxin that binds to a specific ganglioside receptor on intestinal epithelial cells, causing activation of adenylate cyclase and a rise in intracellular cAMP. Which receptor does the cholera toxin primarily bind to in order to exert its effect?

A 6-month-old infant is brought to the pediatric clinic with hypotonia, seizures, and developmental delay. Physical examination reveals hepatomegaly, facial dysmorphism, and failure to thrive. Genetic testing confirms Zellweger syndrome, a peroxisomal biogenesis disorder. Which of the following is most likely to accumulate in this child?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Very long chain fatty acid

questions.stem: A 90-kg man is noted to be gradually gaining weight. After eating a carbohydrate-rich meal, insulin secretion rises, promoting fatty acid synthesis in the liver. Certain enzymes and intermediates become active in this fed state, favoring fat storage. Which of the following are activated in this state, leading to weight gain?Malonyl-CoAAcetyl-CoA carboxylaseMitochondrial carnitine transporterTricarboxylate (citrate) transporter

A 2-day-old male neonate presents with poor feeding, recurrent vomiting, lethargy, and metabolic acidosis. His elder sibling died at 1 week of age with similar complaints. The pediatrician suspects an inborn error of metabolism (IEM) and wants to perform a newborn screening test that can rapidly detect multiple amino acid, organic acid, and fatty acid metabolism disorders from a single blood spot sample. Which of the following investigations is the best screening tool for such metabolic disorders?

An infant presented to the OPD with a history of vomiting and poor feeding. Musty odor is present in the baby's sweat and urine. Guthrie test was done and it was found to be positive. All are true regarding this disease except:

options.label: B
options.text: White patch of hair due to tryptophan deficiency

questions.answerText: White patch of hair due to tryptophan deficiency
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) White patch of hair due to tryptophan deficiency

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy is undergoing genetic evaluation for a suspected metabolic disorder. Genetic sequencing reveals a point mutation in one of his enzymes, where glutamine at a specific position has been replaced by another amino acid. The physician explains to the parents that not all amino acid substitutions will significantly affect the structure or function of the protein, especially if the substituted amino acid has similar chemical properties. Which of the following substitutions is most likely to have no significant effect on the function of the protein product?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Glutamine replaced by asparagine

questions.stem: Glycine is not required in synthesis of.

A mother has brought her 3-month-old baby to the pediatrician and indicates that the infant is lethargic and has poor suckling and seems uninterested in eating. In addition, the mother notes that the baby’s diapers often smell like burnt sugar. This infant likely has a defect in which of the following enzymes?

A 45-year-old man presents to the genetics clinic with a suspected inherited metabolic disorder. The physician wants to analyze a protein sample from the patient to determine its molecular mass and obtain information about its primary amino acid sequence. Which of the following laboratory techniques would be the most appropriate?

A researcher is studying a transcription factor mutation in a patient with an inherited metabolic disorder. The transcription factor binds to DNA to regulate gene expression. Normally, DNA–protein interactions are stabilized by several non-covalent forces. Which of the following types of interaction is not typically involved in DNA–protein binding?

A young couple bring their infant for evaluation. They report that although the baby appears healthy, his urine consistently darkens to black on standing in the diaper pail overnight. On examination, the child is well and thriving. The pediatrician suspects an inborn error of metabolism involving defective degradation of aromatic amino acids. Which amino acid pathway is most likely affected?

options.label: D
options.text: The leucine, isoleucine, and valine pathway

questions.stem: An adolescent female develops hemiballismus after anesthesia for a routine operation. She is tall and lanky, and it is noted that she and her sister both had previous operations for dislocated lenses of the eyes. The symptoms are suspicious for the disease homocystinuria. Which of the following statements is descriptive of this disease?

options.label: A
options.text: Patients may be treated with dietary supplements of vitamin B12

options.label: B
options.text: Patients may be treated with dietary supplements of vitamin C

options.label: C
options.text: There is deficient excretion of homocysteine

options.label: D
options.text: There is a defect in the ability to form cystathionine from homocysteine and serine

questions.answerText: There is a defect in the ability to form cystathionine from homocysteine and serine
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) There is a defect in the ability to form cystathionine from homocysteine and serine

questions.stem: As part of a standard neonatal screen, an infant is diagnosed with a loss of function genetic defect in the enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase. Defects in this enzyme can result in a condition known as phenylketonuria (PKU), which results from the toxic effects of phenylalanine derived phenylketones. Fortunately, this condition can be managed by regulating the amount of phenylalanine provided in the diet. Which of the following nonessential amino acids will need to be supplied in the diet of this infant?

A 7-year-old child presents with growth retardation, dry skin, and lethargy. Laboratory tests reveal low levels of circulating thyroid hormones. The endocrinologist explains that thyroid hormones are synthesized from a specific essential amino acid in the thyroid gland. Which of the following essential amino acids is the precursor for thyroid hormone synthesis?
Type I Tyrosinemia is caused by:
Which of the following molecules serves as the obligate allosteric activator of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (CPS-1) in the urea cycle?

questions.stemHtml: A man presents with diarrhea, dementia, and dermatitis. On examination, he has hyperpigmented, scaly lesions around the neck giving a “Casal’s necklace” appearance (shown in the image). Laboratory evaluation reveals increased 24-hour urinary 5-HIAA (5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

questions.stem: A 6-month-old infant is admitted with poor feeding, vomiting, and irritability. Laboratory evaluation reveals severe hyperammonemia. The child’s elder sibling died in infancy due to a similar illness. The pediatrician starts treatment with sodium benzoate as part of the management plan. What is the mechanism by which benzoic acid helps in this condition?

options.label: A
options.text: It provides an alternative route for N₂ excretion through the N-acetyl glucuronic acid conjugate kynurenine

options.label: B
options.text: It neutralizes NH₃ in both blood as well as urine

options.label: C
options.text: It provides an alternative route for N₂ excretion through glycine conjugate, hippuric acid

questions.answerText: It provides an alternative route for N₂ excretion through glycine conjugate, hippuric acid
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) It provides an alternative route for N₂ excretion through glycine conjugate, hippuric acid

questions.stem: A 60-year-old patient presents with excessive bleeding after minor surgery. Laboratory studies indicate a defect in fibrin formation. The clinician explains that certain amino acids in fibrinopeptides contribute to their chemical properties, including charge interactions important for clot formation. Which of the following amino acids is primarily responsible for the negative charge in fibrinopeptide A?

questions.stemHtml: In this transamination reaction (right), which of the following are the products X and Y

questions.stem: A 2-day-old female infant, previously healthy, is brought to the pediatric ICU due to poor feeding and intermittent lethargy. Around 56 hours of life, she develops focal twitching of her right arm. Laboratory tests show plasma ammonia 887 µmol/L (normal 5–35 µmol/L). Plasma amino acids reveal markedly elevated citrulline but normal argininosuccinate. Which of the following enzyme deficiencies is most consistent with this presentation?

A 45-year-old patient presents with macrocytic anemia, positive Romberg sign, and peripheral neuropathy. Laboratory tests reveal elevated homocysteine levels. Considering the biochemical role of vitamin B12, which of the following amino acids is most likely deficient in this patient?

questions.stemHtml: In the TCA cycle, the enzyme Aconitase can be inhibited by fluoroacetate. A graph below shows the activity of Aconitase with and without fluoroacetate, represented as a double reciprocal plot. The effect of fluoroacetate on the kinetic parameters of Aconitase is indicated by:

options.label: D
options.text: Increase in both Km and Vmax

questions.stem: Lactate dehydrogenase is an enzyme found in nearly all living cells. LDH catalyzes the conversion of lactate to pyruvate and back, as it converts NAD+ to NADH and back. What is the best suited statement for isoenzyme?

options.label: C
options.text: Multimeric enzymes with different subunit composition, different electrophoretic properties but similar functions

questions.answerText: Multimeric enzymes with different subunit composition, different electrophoretic properties but similar functions
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Multimeric enzymes with different subunit composition, different electrophoretic properties but similar functions

questions.stem: In an enzyme kinetics experiment, the substrate concentration is maintained at a level significantly higher than the Km​, effectively saturating the enzyme. Under these conditions, 1% of the substrate is converted into 20 µmol of product in 10 minutes using a fixed amount of enzyme. In a second experiment, half the enzyme amount is used, but the substrate concentration increased to Double of previous experiment. How long would it take to produce the same amount (20 µmol) of product in this modified experiment?

questions.stemHtml: A research study examines the effect of an inhibitor on the enzyme kinetics of a metabolic reaction. The Lineweaver-Burk plot of the reaction is analyzed, showing two lines: one for the enzyme activity without the inhibitor and the other with the inhibitor. Based on this information, what type of enzyme inhibition is being represented in this plot?

questions.stem: A 40-year-old chronic alcoholic presents with confusion, ataxia, and ophthalmoplegia. Blood work shows evidence of thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency. This vitamin is required in the form of thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) as a coenzyme. Deficiency of TPP results in decreased energy production primarily because TPP:

options.label: A
options.text: Interferes with energy production from amino acids

options.label: B
options.text: Is coenzyme for pyruvate and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase

questions.answerText: Is coenzyme for pyruvate and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Is coenzyme for pyruvate and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase

questions.stem: A 12-year-old boy presents with muscle cramps and fatigue during exercise. Biochemical evaluation suggests impaired glycogenolysis due to defective glycogen phosphorylase activity. Which of the following vitamins, acting as a cofactor, is essential for the normal function of glycogen phosphorylase?

A 6-month-old infant is brought to the emergency department with recurrent convulsions, irritability, and failure to thrive. On evaluation, the physician suspects pyridoxine (vitamin B6) deficiency, which can lead to defective neurotransmitter synthesis (↓ GABA). Which of the following biochemical tests is most appropriate to confirm vitamin B6 deficiency?

A 3-year-old boy presents with dilated cardiomyopathy, skeletal muscle weakness, neutropenia, and recurrent infections. Genetic testing confirms Barth syndrome, an X-linked disorder caused by defective cardiolipin synthesis. Cardiolipin is an important phospholipid found in the membranes of which of the following organelles?

A 5-year-old child presents with recurrent infections, pallor, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, and hypertonia. During hospitalization, the child develops fatal bronchopneumonia. Bone marrow biopsy reveals cells with a “crumpled tissue paper” appearance. Which of the following is most likely to accumulate in this condition?
A 45-year-old man presents laboratory reports showing low insulin: glucagon ratio. Which of the following metabolic pathways will be most favored in this state?

A 21-year-old vegetarian presents with complaints of low mood and poor sleep. On further evaluation, the physician explains that his symptoms may be related to deficiency of an essential amino acid that serves as a precursor for serotonin, melatonin, and niacin. This amino acid is both glucogenic and ketogenic. Which of the following best describes this amino acid?

options.label: D
options.text: Polar, essential and both glucogenic & ketogenic

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Nonpolar, essential, both glucogenic & ketogenic

questions.stem: A 24-year-old medical student is revising the genetic code. He recalls that the code is degenerate, meaning that most amino acids are coded by more than one codon. However, a few amino acids are exceptions and are encoded by only a single codon. Which of the following amino acids does not show degeneracy of the genetic code?

A 6-year-old boy presents with megaloblastic anemia that does not improve with vitamin B12 or folate supplementation. Genetic testing reveals a defect in the enzyme involved in pyrimidine synthesis. Laboratory findings show increased urinary excretion of orotic acid. Which of the following statements about orotic acid is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Can be converted to UMP and CTP

options.label: B
options.text: Reacts with PRPP to form OMP

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy of middle eastern ancestry is known to have inherited favism, a sensitivity to fava beans due to glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency (MIM305900). Which of the following indicates the primary pathway affected by this deficiency and the pathway secondarily affected because one of its energy substrates will be deficient?

options.label: A
options.text: Pentose phosphate pathway, fatty acid synthesis

options.label: B
options.text: Pentose phosphate pathway, fatty acid oxidation

options.label: C
options.text: Citric acid cycle, Pentose phosphate pathway

questions.answerText: Pentose phosphate pathway, fatty acid synthesis
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Pentose phosphate pathway, fatty acid synthesis

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man with a strong family history of premature heart disease presents for a routine health check-up. His lipid profile shows normal total cholesterol and triglyceride levels, but his lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is significantly elevated. Which condition is he most predisposed to due to this abnormality?

A 10-year-old boy from a rural part of China presents with progressive fatigue, palpitations, and swelling of the legs. Echocardiography shows cardiomyopathy. The local population is known to consume food grown in soil deficient in a particular micronutrient. Which deficiency is the most likely cause of his condition, known as Keshan disease?
Cytosolic Cytochrome C mediates?

A 58-year-old patient has been on long-term hydrochlorothiazide therapy for hypertension. He presents with fatigue, symmetrical tingling in the hands and feet, and signs of heart failure. Laboratory tests show no evidence of anemia. Which of the following nutrient deficiencies is most likely responsible for his clinical presentation?

A 15-month-old female child whose growth rate has been in the low over the last year presents with chronic, nonproductive cough for which she was prescribed antibiotics and taking for long time patient has diarrhea with foul-smelling stools. She is diagnosed as having cystic fibrosis. For which of the following vitamins is this child most likely to be at risk of deficiency?

30-year-old man presented at clinic with a history of intermittent abdominal pain and episodes of confusion and psychiatric problems. Laboratory tests revealed increases of urinary δ-aminolevulinate and porphobilinogen. Mutational analysis revealed a mutation in the gene for uroporphyrinogen I synthase (porphobilinogen deaminase). The probable diagnosis was:

A 45-year-old man with a long history of chronic alcoholism presents to the emergency department after experiencing confusion, sweating, and tremors following a night of heavy drinking after a day of strenuous exercise without food intake. Laboratory tests reveal significantly low blood glucose levels, indicating hypoglycemia. The physician explains that alcohol can disrupt normal metabolic processes in the liver, leading to impaired glucose production. Which of the following metabolic pathways is primarily inhibited by alcohol consumption, contributing to the patient's hypoglycemia?
How do Di-Deoxy nucleotides (For eg. 2’3’ dideoxy ATP) inhibit viral DNA replication by reverse transcriptase?

options.label: A
options.text: There is no 2’ Hydroxyl group to form the next phosphodiester bond

options.label: B
options.text: There is no 3’ Hydroxyl group to form the next phosphodiester bond

options.label: C
options.text: The analog can not make hydrogen bond to DNA template

options.label: D
options.text: Incorporation of the analog initiates rapid degradation of newly synthesized strand

questions.answerText: There is no 3’ Hydroxyl group to form the next phosphodiester bond
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) There is no 3’ Hydroxyl group to form the next phosphodiester bond

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man presents with elevated cholesterol and triglyceride levels on lipid profile testing. questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy is being evaluated for growth delay and developmental abnormalities. Laboratory studies suggest impaired collagen synthesis. During teaching rounds, the attending physician asks the medical students to recall which amino acids require an aminoacyl-tRNA for their incorporation during protein synthesis on the ribosome. The students are reminded that some amino acids found in proteins are not directly inserted during translation but are instead post-translationally modified. Which of the following amino acids does not require aminoacyl-tRNA during protein synthesis?

The 5-year-old son of a migrant worker is brought to a clinic with chills, headache, nausea, vomiting, and sore throat. The examining physician notes a persistent grayish colored membrane near the tonsils. History reveals that the patient has not been immunized against diphtheria. Diphtheria toxin is potentially lethal in this unimmunized patient because it causes which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Inactivates an elongation factor required for translocation in protein synthesis

options.label: B
options.text: Binds to the ribosome and prevents peptide bond formation

options.label: C
options.text: Prevents binding of mRNA to the 60S ribosomal subunit

questions.answerText: Inactivates an elongation factor required for translocation in protein synthesis
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Inactivates an elongation factor required for translocation in protein synthesis

questions.stem: A couple with a strong family history of sickle cell anemia undergo genetic counseling. The geneticist suggests performing restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP) analysis to track inheritance of the disease allele. questions.stem: The production of mRNA in eukaryotic cells requires a large number of steps, and drugs targeted to any of these steps could block mRNA production. Which one of the following accurately describes a part of the process of producing mRNA from a eukaryotic gene?

options.label: A
options.text: The sense strand of DNA is the strand used by RNA polymerase during transcription.

options.label: B
options.text: The antisense DNA strand is identical to the RNA transcript except that the DNA strand contains thymine and the RNA strand contains uracil.

options.label: C
options.text: The first RNA form produced contains both intron and exon sequences.

options.label: D
options.text: Mature mRNA contains a cap at the 5′-end, a poly (A) tail at the 3′ end, introns, and exons.

questions.answerText: The first RNA form produced contains both intron and exon sequences.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) The first RNA form produced contains both intron and exon sequences
